title: Copy a practice file
summary: cp makes another copy of a file. Give a new destination name when you want to preserve both versions.
introduction: cp makes another copy of a file. Give a new destination name when you want to preserve both versions. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: cp makes another copy of a file. Give a new destination name when you want to preserve both versions.
The copy has the same text at the moment cp ran. Later edits to one file do not automatically update the other.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Append a line to the copy and compare both files.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: cp may replace an existing destination; choose a fresh practice name.
For more detail later, use this [Linux further reading](https://www.gnu.org/software/coreutils/manual/coreutils.html).
